h: In Midrash Tanchuma there: You find that whoever is meticulous

p: בְּתַנְחוּמָא שָׁם:
In Midrash Tanchuma there:
"אַתָּה מוֹצֵא כָּל הַמְדַקְדֵּק עַל הַמִּצְווֹת שְׂכָרוֹ מְרוּבֶּה,
You find that whoever is meticulous with the commandments, his reward is abundant,
שֶׁכֵּן מָצִינוּ בְּאַבְרָהָם שֶׁדִּקְדֵּק עַל הַמִּצְווֹת, לְפִיכָךְ נִקְרָא אוֹהֲבוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא וְכוּלֵי,
for so we find with Avraham who was meticulous with the mitzvot, wherefore he was titled the lover of the Holy One, etc.,
אֲפִילּוּ עֵירוּבֵי תַבְשִׁילִין שָׁמַר וְכוּלֵי;
even the rabbinic ordinance of Eruv Tavshilin he observed, etc.;
'וְתוֹרֹתָי' – וְכִי תוֹרוֹת הַרְבֵּה וְכוּלֵי?
''and My torot'—are there many torot?'
אֵלּוּ דִּקְדּוּקֵי מִצְווֹת וְכוּלֵי",
These are the minutiae of the commandments, etc.'
הַיְינוּ תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה נִקְרְאוּ דִּקְדּוּקֵי מִצְווֹת.
meaning that the Oral Torah is specifically titled 'the minutiae of the commandments.'
שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב נִזְכְּרָה רַק כְּלַל הַמִּצְוָה,
For in the Written Torah only the general principle of the commandment is mentioned,
וּבַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה נִסְדַּר עַל זֶה מַסֶּכֶת שְׁלֵימָה וַהֲלָכוֹת מְרוּבּוֹת;
whereas in the Oral Torah there is formulated upon it an entire tractate and numerous detailed halakhot;
וְזֶה שֶׁלָּמַד מִ"תּוֹרֹתָי" לְשׁוֹן רַבִּים עַל תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה.
and this explains why he derived from 'My torot' in the plural an exposition upon the Oral Torah.
וְכֵן כָּתַב בְּמִדְרַשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא לְעֵיל פָּרָשַׁת נֹחַ:
And so wrote Midrash Tanchuma earlier in Parashat Noach:
"וְנָתַן לָנוּ תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב בְּרֶמֶז, וּפֵירְשׁוּם בַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה וְכוּלֵי,
''And He gave us the Written Torah in allusion, and they explicated them in the Oral Torah, etc.,
תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב כְּלָלוֹת וְתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה פְּרָטוֹת וְכוּלֵי",
the Written Torah being generalizations and the Oral Torah particularizations, etc.,'
וְאָמַר אַחַר כָּךְ עַל תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
and he stated afterward regarding the Oral Torah
שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהּ דִּקְדּוּקֵי מִצְווֹת קַלּוֹת וַחֲמוּרוֹת וְכוּלֵי,
that it contains the fine minutiae of commandments, light and stringent, etc.,
שֶׁאֵין לוֹמֵד אוֹתָהּ אֶלָּא מִי שֶׁאוֹהֵב הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בְּכָל לִבּוֹ וּבְכָל נַפְשׁוֹ וּבְכָל מְאֹדוֹ וְכוּלֵי, עַיֵּין שָׁם.
which is studied solely by one who loves the Holy One with all his heart, soul, and might, see there.

paragraphs.text: Mesillas Yesharim 18:9–12: “One who truly loves the Creator, blessed be His Name, will not strive and aim merely to discharge his obligation through what is already well known as the duty incumbent on all Israel. Rather, he will act like a son who loves his father: if his father reveals even a little of his wish for something, the son will already do as much as he can in that matter and that action. Even though his father said it only once, and in half a sentence, that is enough for the son to understand the direction of his father’s wishes and to do even what he did not expressly tell him, whenever he can infer for himself that it will give his father satisfaction. He will not wait for a more explicit command or for his father to repeat it. We see this arise before our eyes at every time and hour between loving companions, between a man and his wife, and between a father and son—in general, between any people whose mutual love is truly strong. Such a person will not say, “I was not commanded further; what I was expressly commanded is enough for me.” Rather, from what he was commanded he will infer the intention of the one who commanded, and will strive to do whatever he can infer will give that person satisfaction. The same will happen to one who faithfully loves his Creator, for he too belongs among those who love. The mitzvos whose commands are explicit and well known will serve him as a disclosure of His intention, showing that His blessed will and desire incline toward that matter. He will then not say, “What was expressly stated is enough for me,” or, “I shall discharge my obligation by doing the minimum incumbent on me.” On the contrary, he will say: “Since I have found and seen that His blessed desire inclines this way, this will guide me to do more in this matter and to extend it in every direction that I can infer His blessed will desires.” This is what is called giving satisfaction to one’s Maker.”

p: וְאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, שֶׁהָיְתָה מִדָּתוֹ הָאַהֲבָה כְּמַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "זֶרַע אַבְרָהָם אֹהֲבִי",
And Avraham our Father, peace be upon him, whose attribute was Love, as stated: 'the seed of Avraham who loved Me,'
שָׁמַר כָּל דִּקְדּוּקֵי מִצְווֹת, שֶׁהוּא כָּל דִּקְדּוּקֵי סוֹפְרִים,
observed all minutiae of the commandments, which are the rabbinic stringencies,
כְּמוֹ עֵירוּבֵי תַבְשִׁילִין שֶׁהוּא כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּבְרוֹר מָנָה יָפָה לְשַׁבָּת (בֵּיצָה טז עַמּוּד ב).
such as Eruv Tavshilin whose purpose is that one select a choice portion for Shabbat (Beitzah 16b).
וּבְאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ הָיְתָה כָּל הַתּוֹרָה בְּגֶדֶר תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
And in Avraham our Father the entire Torah existed within the category of Oral Torah,
כֵּיוָן שֶׁלֹּא נִצְטַוָּה עָלֶיהָ,
since he had not yet been formally commanded concerning it,
רַק שֶׁזִּימֵּן לוֹ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שְׁתֵּי כִלְיוֹתָיו כְּמִין שְׁנֵי רַבָּנִים וּמְלַמְּדוֹת אוֹתוֹ תּוֹרָה וְחָכְמָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה סא);
only that Hashem provided him his two kidneys like two rabbis instructing him in Torah and wisdom (Bereishit Rabbah 61);
וְכָל עֵסֶק אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ וְכָל מַעֲשָׂיו הָיוּ רַק דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה,
and all of Avraham's occupations and deeds were strictly words of Torah,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁלָּמַד בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (סִטְרֵי תּוֹרָה פח עַמּוּד א):
and as the holy Zohar derived (Sitrei Torah 88a):
"'אַחַר הַדְּבָרִים הָאֵלֶּה' – אִלֵּין פִּתְגָּמֵי אוֹרַיְיתָא,
''After these things (devarim)'—these are the words of Torah,
דִּכְתִיב: 'אֵת הַדְּבָרִים הָאֵלֶּה דִּבֶּר ה' וְגוֹמֵר',
for it is written: 'These words Hashem spoke, etc.,'
מַה לְּהַלָּן פִּתְגָּמֵי אוֹרַיְיתָא, אוּף הָכָא פִּתְגָּמֵי אוֹרַיְיתָא",
just as there it denotes words of Torah, so here it denotes words of Torah,'
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁלָּמַד שֶׁכָּל עִנְיַן אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם וּמִלְחַמְתּוֹ עִם הַמְּלָכִים הָיָה דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה.
meaning he derived that the entire episode of Avraham and his battle against the four kings was purely words of Torah.

h: The Gemara’s teaching and the written and oral Torah

p: וְזֶה עִנְיַן מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ בַּגְּמָרָא (נְדָרִים לב עַמּוּד א):
And this explains what is stated in the Gemara (Nedarim 32a):
"'וַיָּרֶק אֶת חֲנִיכָיו' – שֶׁהוֹרִיקָן בַּתּוֹרָה",
“'He armed his trained men'—he emptied/equipped them in Torah,”
וּפֵירֵשׁ רַשִּׁ"י: שֶׁלִּמְּדָם תּוֹרָה וְכוּלֵי.
and Rashi explained: that he taught them Torah, etc.
וְלִכְאוֹרָה, בַּמִּלְחָמָה הָא לֹא לִמְּדָם תּוֹרָה, וְאַדְּרַבָּה, בִּיטְּלָם מִתַּלְמוּד תּוֹרָה,
Now seemingly, in actual warfare he did not teach them Torah, but on the contrary, drew them away from study,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּגְּמָרָא מִקּוֹדֶם שֶׁנֶּעֱנַשׁ מִפְּנֵי שֶׁעָשָׂה אַנְגַּרְיָא בְּתַלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים;
and as the Gemara stated earlier: that he was punished because he drafted Torah scholars into forced military service;
וְהָרַ"ן זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה בְּפֵירוּשׁ לָשׁוֹן אַחֵר: שֶׁהוֹרִיקָן מֵהַתּוֹרָה שֶׁעָשָׂה בָּהֶם אַנְגַּרְיָא.
and the Ran of blessed memory in a secondary explanation explains: that he emptied them out of Torah by conscripting them.
אַךְ פֵּירוּשׁ רַשִּׁ"י שֶׁלִּמְּדָם תּוֹרָה יֵשׁ לְהָבִין.
Yet Rashi's commentary that he taught them Torah requires understanding.
אַךְ הַמְּכֻוָּון שֶׁזֵּירְזָן בְּמַה שֶּׁלִּמְּדָם שֶׁכָּל עֵסֶק מִלְחַמְתּוֹ דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה,
Rather, the intention is that he galvanized them by teaching that the entire campaign was words of Torah,
וְכָאָמוּר שֶׁכָּל מַעֲשֵׂי הָאָבוֹת הָיוּ רַק דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה,
for all deeds of the Patriarchs were solely words of Torah,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁלָּמַד בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ מִגְּזֵירָה שָׁוָה מִפָּסוּק "אֵת הַדְּבָרִים הָאֵלֶּה וְגוֹמֵר",
as the holy Zohar deduced via verbal analogy (gezeirah shavah) from the verse 'These words, etc.'
דִּכְתִיב בְּמַתַּן תּוֹרָה אַחַר דִּבְּרוֹת שְׁנִיּוֹת,
which is written at the Giving of the Torah following the second tablets,
וְלֹא לָמַד מִדִּכְתִיב בְּדִבְּרוֹת רִאשׁוֹנוֹת "וַיְדַבֵּר אֱלֹהִים אֵת כָּל הַדְּבָרִים הָאֵלֶּה".
and did not deduce it from the first tablets where it says: 'And God spoke all these words.'

h: The explanation is as we stated: that all Torah in Avraham

p: אַךְ הָעִנְיָן כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ,
Rather, the explanation is as we stated:
שֶׁכָּל הַתּוֹרָה הָיְתָה אֵצֶל אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בְּגֶדֶר תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה כֵּיוָן שֶׁלֹּא נִצְטַוָּה;
that all Torah in Avraham our Father existed as Oral Torah since he had not been commanded;
וְאִיתָא בִּמְדְרַשׁ רַבָּה (תִּשָּׂא פָּרָשָׁה מו וּפָרָשָׁה מז):
and it is taught in Midrash Rabbah (Ki Tisa 46 and 47):
"אַל תִּצְטַעֵר שֶׁבַּלּוּחוֹת הָרִאשׁוֹנוֹת לֹא הָיוּ אֶלָּא עֲשֶׂרֶת הַדִּבְּרוֹת בִּלְבַד,
Do not grieve, for in the first tablets there were only the Ten Commandments alone,
וּבַלּוּחוֹת שְׁנִיּוֹת אֲנִי נוֹתֵן לְךָ שֶׁיְּהֵא בָּהֶן הֲלָכוֹת, מִדְרָשׁ וְאַגָּדוֹת", עַיֵּין שָׁם.
while in the second tablets I give you that there be included halakhot, midrash, and aggadot, see there.
וְזֶה שֶׁלָּמַד בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ הַגְּזֵירָה שָׁוָה מֵ"הַדְּבָרִים הָאֵלֶּה" דִּכְתִיב אַחַר דִּבְּרוֹת שְׁנִיּוֹת,
And this is why the holy Zohar drew the analogy from 'these words' written after the second tablets,
שֶׁנִּכְלַל בָּהֶן תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה;
in which the Oral Torah was fully enveloped;
וְכֵן כָּל עִנְיְנֵי אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם וּמִלְחַמְתּוֹ הָיוּ דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, וְהַיְינוּ תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה.
and likewise all affairs of Avraham and his battle were words of Torah, namely the Oral Torah.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Lech Lecha 7: ““I have raised my hand to God,” and so forth. Why did Abraham our father refuse to benefit from the king of Sodom, although we find that he accepted gifts from Pharaoh and Abimelech? His undertaking to rescue Lot required clarification. Lot contained a good power, since Naamah the Ammonite and Ruth the Moabite would descend from him; the rest was evil, since Ammon and Moab descended from him, as explained. Abraham had to clarify within himself that, in its depth, his entire intention was only to rescue those two good offshoots. Wherever a person requires clarification, the counsel is first to remove all personal interests in his own benefit. h: The Zohar’s teaching and the written and oral Torah

p: אַךְ בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ג, רסד עַמּוּד א) אִיתָא:
Yet in the holy Zohar (III, 264a) it is taught:
"תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב – דָּא הוּא דִּכְתִיב הֲוָיָ"ה; תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה – דִּכְתִיב אֱלֹהִים וְכוּלֵי, דָּא כְּלָל וְדָא פְּרָט", עַיֵּין שָׁם;
''The Written Torah—that is where Havayah is written; the Oral Torah—where Elohim is written, etc., this is general and this is particular,'' see there;
וְכֵן כָּתַב בְּרַעְיָא מְהֵימְנָא (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב, כה עַמּוּד א):
and so wrote in Ra'aya Meheimna (Zohar II, 25a):
"כִּי ה' הוּא הָאֱלֹהִים – דָּא בְּאֹרַח פְּרָט וְכוּלֵי",
''For Hashem He is God'—this is by way of particularization, etc.,'
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּתַנְחוּמָא: תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב כְּלָלוֹת וְתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה פְּרָטוֹת.
and as written in Tanchuma: Written Torah is generalizations and Oral Torah is details.
וְאִם כֵּן צָרִיךְ לְהָבִין, לָמָּה בְּדִבְּרוֹת רִאשׁוֹנוֹת כְּתִיב: "וַיְדַבֵּר אֱלֹהִים אֵת כָּל הַדְּבָרִים וְגוֹמֵר",
And if so, one must understand: why in the first tablets is it written 'And Elohim spoke all these words, etc.,'
וְאַחַר דִּבְּרוֹת שְׁנִיּוֹת כְּתִיב: "אֶת הַדְּבָרִים הָאֵלֶּה דִּבֶּר ה' וְגוֹמֵר"?
whereas after the second tablets it is written: 'These words Hashem spoke, etc.'?
וְאִיפְּכָא הֲוָה לֵיהּ לְמִכְתַּב לְפִי הָאָמוּר,
And seemingly the reverse should have been written according to the aforesaid,
דְּדִבְּרוֹת שְׁנִיּוֹת נִכְלַל עִמָּהֶם כָּל תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה!
since with the second tablets all of the Oral Torah was incorporated!

They unite with one another and all becomes one. Therefore the totality of Torah embraces above and below, for this name is above and that name is below: this is the mystery of the upper world and that of the lower world. Therefore it is written: “You were shown to know that the Lord is God.” This is the totality of everything, and a person must know all that we have said in this world.”

p: אֲבָל יוּבַן עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה יִשָּׁקֵנִי):
However, this will be understood through what is taught in the Midrash (Shir HaShirim Rabbah, Parashat Yishakeni):
בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁשָּׁמְעוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל "אָנֹכִי ה' אֱלֹהֶיךָ" נִתְקַע תַּלְמוּד תּוֹרָה בְּלִבָּם וְכוּלֵי,
at the moment Israel heard 'I am Hashem your God,' the study of Torah was driven deeply into their hearts, etc.,
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁאָז נִתְקַע תַּלְמוּד תּוֹרָה בְּלִבָּם שֶׁיָּדְעוּ מִמַּאֲמַר "אָנֹכִי" אַף הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
meaning that then the study of Torah was embedded in their hearts such that they knew from the utterance 'I am' even the Oral Torah,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לֶעָתִיד, דִּכְתִיב: "וְלֹא יְלַמְּדוּ עוֹד אִישׁ אֶת רֵעֵהוּ וְגוֹמֵר כִּי כוּלָּם יֵדְעוּ אוֹתִי וְגוֹמֵר".
just as will be in the ultimate future, as written: 'and they shall teach no more every man his neighbor... for they shall all know Me, etc.' (Jeremiah 31:33).
וּבְדִבּוּר "אָנֹכִי" כָּל הַתּוֹרָה,
And within the single utterance 'I am' the entire Torah is subsumed,
דְּכָל תַּרְיַ"ג מִצְווֹת נִקְרָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב, פב עַמּוּד ב) "תַּרְיַ"ג עֵיטִין",
for all 613 commandments are termed in the holy Zohar (II, 82b) '613 advices',
וְהַיְינוּ עֵצוֹת שֶׁיִּכָּנֵס מַאֲמַר "אָנֹכִי" וְיָאִיר בַּלֵּב.
meaning spiritual directives to enable the proclamation 'I am' to enter and radiate within the heart.
וּבַגְּמָרָא (נְדָרִים כב עַמּוּד ב):
And in the Gemara (Nedarim 22b):
"אִלְמָלֵא חָטְאוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל, לֹא נִיתַּן לָהֶם אֶלָּא חֲמִשָּׁה חוּמְשֵׁי תוֹרָה וְכוּלֵי",
'Had Israel not sinned, they would have been given only the Five Books of the Torah, etc.,'
שֶׁהָיוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל מַשִּׂיגִין כָּל סִתְרֵי תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה גַּם כֵּן מִתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב;
for Israel would have comprehended all esoteric mysteries of the Oral Torah directly from the Written Torah;

Whereas in the second tablets, which were given after the fall of the Golden Calf,
וְהוּצְרְכוּ לְתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה "הַרְבֵּה חָכְמָה" לְתַקֵּן "הַרְבֵּה כָּעַס",
and they required the Oral Torah as 'much wisdom' to repair 'much anger,'
כְּתִיב: "אֶת הַדְּבָרִים הָאֵלֶּה דִּבֶּר ה' וְגוֹמֵר",
it is written: 'These words Hashem spoke, etc.,'
לְהוֹרוֹת שֶׁאַף שֶׁנִּיתַּן לָהֶם הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, מִדְרָשׁ, הֲלָכוֹת וְאַגָּדוֹת, הַרְבֵּה חָכְמָה,
to demonstrate that even though the Oral Torah was given to them—midrash, halakhot, and aggadot, 'much wisdom'—
מִכָּל מָקוֹם הַכֹּל הוּא מִשֵּׁם הֲוָיָ"ה,
nonetheless all derives from the Name Havayah,
שֶׁהַכֹּל הוּא כָּלוּל בַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב, וְהֵם "דְּבָרַי אֲשֶׁר שַׂמְתִּי בְּפִיךָ".
for everything is included in the Written Torah, these being 'My words which I have put in your mouth' (Isaiah 59:21).

The holy Zohar explains that additional letters vav appear in the second Decalogue, indicating that the disclosure was less direct. Following the first tablets, Israel’s heart had become elevated beyond its bounds, and they made the calf, as explained in Ki Tissa. This is what the Ari’s Likkutei Torah says: the first tablets were from the foundation of Imma, signifying the exceptional love called “your mother’s Torah”; therefore they were broken. The second tablets came from the light of Abba, from the mystery of awe, through measured stages, restfulness, and proper conduct, called “your father’s discipline.” Because their great inward love was surrounded by a garment of awe, they endured.”

reviewedSourceExcerpt.en: So too with the first tablets, in which the blessed God showed Israel exceptional affection, as we explained elsewhere concerning the difference between the first and later tablets. The holy Zohar explains that additional letters vav appear in the second Decalogue, indicating that the disclosure was less direct. Following the first tablets, Israel’s heart had become elevated beyond its bounds, and they made the calf, as explained in Ki Tissa. This is what the Ari’s Likkutei Torah says: the first tablets were from the foundation of Imma, signifying the exceptional love called “your mother’s Torah”; therefore they were broken. The second tablets came from the light of Abba, from the mystery of awe, through measured stages, restfulness, and proper conduct, called “your father’s discipline.” Because their great inward love was surrounded by a garment of awe, they endured.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Machshavot Charutz 12:9: “On Yom Kippur the later tablets were given. They are the repair after the damage and the departure from the ordered course; from there Oral Torah draws its nourishment. As is known, “Remember” belongs to the masculine, and “Guard” to the feminine, and the second tablets belong to the feminine mystery. In the future, when all Oral Torah reaches completion, it too will become Written Torah: these are the later tablets. Written Torah corresponds to the first tablets, which for now are the broken tablets resting in the Ark. Then, when “He swallows up death forever,” the first tablets too will return to their former state, as stated in the Tikkunim: death is the mystery of the breaking of the tablets. “The light of the moon will be like the light of the sun”—the tablets of Written Torah—and “the light of the sun will be sevenfold, like the light of the seven days,” by which a person could see from one end of the world to the other. This is the light of the first tablets, through which there was freedom from the angel of death and the evil inclination, as in the future, when there will no longer be any separating barrier that conceals the light.”

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Tiferet Yosef, Vayeilech and Shabbat Shuvah 3: “This mitzvah [writing the Torah] is the last of the 613 mitzvot. The holy Zohar calls the 613 mitzvot “the 613 counsels of Torah.” My revered father, of blessed memory, asked: counsels toward what? paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Sod Yesharim, Yom Kippur 48:1: “Only after the first tablets were broken, when it appeared to Israel that this supernal holiness had departed from them and that they had lost it completely, God forbid, did the blessed God restore to Israel, through the later tablets and through the greatness of their outcry and the strength of their service, that very same holiness of the first tablets. Therefore the day on which the later tablets were given is called a festival—a sacred convocation, summoned from the supernal holiness. This is the essential holiness of the first tablets, which is fixed and enduring from His side, like the holiness of Shabbat that spreads through Israel’s service into the festivals and their appointed times. In the same way, through Israel’s service, the supernal holiness of the first tablets spread into the later tablets. Thus the Zohar explains the verse, “For he has brought a bad name upon a virgin of Israel”: one who brings a bad name upon her by saying that the former Torah is not this Torah because its tablets were broken will be answered by the Holy One, blessed be He. “They shall spread out the garment”: a scroll of the Torah will be opened, and they will see written in it, “Carve for yourself two tablets of stone like the first, and I will write upon the tablets the words that were upon the first tablets which you broke.” The blessed God thereby testifies that the first tablets never departed from Israel, God forbid, and the illumination of their holiness was never damaged, even after they were broken. The first tablets are like “a virgin whom no man has known.” Of one who falsely says that Israel no longer possesses that holiness, it says, “He has brought a bad name upon a virgin of Israel.” Rather, all the essential holiness of the first tablets was clothed within the later tablets.”

Thus the Zohar explains the verse, “For he has brought a bad name upon a virgin of Israel”: one who brings a bad name upon her by saying that the former Torah is not this Torah because its tablets were broken will be answered by the Holy One, blessed be He. “They shall spread out the garment”: a scroll of the Torah will be opened, and they will see written in it, “Carve for yourself two tablets of stone like the first, and I will write upon the tablets the words that were upon the first tablets which you broke.” The blessed God thereby testifies that the first tablets never departed from Israel, God forbid, and the illumination of their holiness was never damaged, even after they were broken. The first tablets are like “a virgin whom no man has known.” Of one who falsely says that Israel no longer possesses that holiness, it says, “He has brought a bad name upon a virgin of Israel.” Rather, all the essential holiness of the first tablets was clothed within the later tablets.

p: וּמִתְּחִלָּה חֲמֵשׁ פְּעָמִים אוֹרָה שֶׁבְּמַאֲמַר "יְהִי אוֹר" כְּנֶגֶד חֲמִשָּׁה חוּמְשֵׁי תוֹרָה (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה),
And initially the five occurrences of light in the utterance 'Let there be light' correspond to the Five Books of the Torah (Bereishit Rabbah),
וְאַחַר כָּךְ נִגְנַז הָאוֹר הָרִאשׁוֹן לְעַמְלֵי תוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (מִדְרַשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא נֹחַ שָׁם);
and subsequently the Primordial Light was concealed for those who toil in the Oral Torah (Midrash Tanchuma, Noach ibid.);
וְהַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, עַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: "תִּזַּל כַּטַּל אִמְרָתִי",
and regarding the Oral Torah Scripture proclaims: 'My speech shall distill as the dew' (Deuteronomy 32:2),
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ, דְּנִדְמֵית תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה כַּטַּל שֶׁאֵינוֹ נִיכָּר כְּשֶׁיּוֹרֵד שֶׁהוּא מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם,
and as we explained, the Oral Torah resembles dew which is not visibly noticed as descending from heaven,
רַק מְבִינִים כְּשֶׁרוֹאִים הָאָרֶץ לַחָה שֶׁיָּרַד הַטַּל;
only recognized when seeing the earth moist that dew has fallen;
וְכֵן תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה נִדְמֶה לַחֲכָמִים שֶׁמְּחַדְּשִׁים בְּלִבָּם,
so too the Oral Torah appears to the sages as if they innovate it from their own heart,
וּבֶאֱמֶת הֵם דְּבַר ה', "דְּבָרַי אֲשֶׁר שַׂמְתִּי בְּפִיךָ",
while in truth they are the word of Hashem: 'My words which I have put in your mouth,'
וְהוּא מִטַּלָּא דְעַתִּיקָא.
and it derives from the Dew of Atika.
וְלָזֶה זָכָה אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ, שֶׁהָיוּ שְׁתֵּי כִלְיוֹתָיו נוֹבְעוֹת חָכְמָה שֶׁזִּימֵּן ה' לוֹ (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה),
And to this Avraham our Father merited, his two kidneys welling with wisdom that Hashem provided him (Bereishit Rabbah),
וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר לוֹ: "לְךָ טַל יַלְדֻתֶךָ".
and this is what was said to him: 'To you is the dew of your youth.'
וְשַׁבָּת הוּא גַּם כֵּן מִדָּה שְׁבִיעִית, מַלְכוּת, "פֶּה", "תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה קָרֵינַן לָהּ",
And Shabbat is likewise the seventh attribute, Malchut, the 'Mouth', 'we title it the Oral Torah',
וְהַזְּמַן לִזְכּוֹת בּוֹ לַתּוֹרָה, וּבִפְרָט בִּסְעוּדָתָא דְעַתִּיקָא.
and the opportune time to merit Torah, particularly during the feast of Atika Kadisha.
